hook: At Twelve, Dickens Worked in a Blacking Factory
text: When Charles Dickens was about twelve, his family's money ran out. He was sent to work in a crumbling old warehouse by the River Thames, overrun with rats. For ten hours a day he covered little pots of boot blacking with paper, tied them with string, and pasted on the labels. That same winter his father was taken to a debtors' prison. For more than twenty years, Dickens told almost nobody about it. But he never forgot. And you can feel that hungry child in nearly every book he wrote.
